sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: Which of these is a famous historical monument in India built entirely of white marble?
What type of renewable energy do we get directly from the light and heat of the Sun?
What is the natural fiber obtained from the fleece of sheep used to make warm winter clothes?
Which season is primarily characterized by the shedding of leaves from deciduous trees?
What is the protective layer in the Earth's atmosphere that blocks harmful ultraviolet solar rays?
Which of the following is considered a non-renewable source of energy that causes pollution?
In textile manufacturing, what is the specific process of making continuous yarn from raw fibers called?
Which vast geographical region is famously known around the world as the 'Roof of the World'?
What is the primary cause of the continuous cycle of day and night on Earth?
options: A) Earth's rotation on its axis
B) Earth's revolution around the Sun
D) The Sun's movement across the sky
questions.answer: A) Earth's rotation on its axis

questions.question_text: Which eco-friendly practice involves converting waste materials into brand new materials and usable objects?
Why is the Great Wall of China considered a unique and significant historical place? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: It is an ancient series of massive walls built across northern China to protect the empire from invaders, making it a globally unique architectural wonder.

questions.question_text: Explain how a modern wind turbine successfully generates clean electrical energy for our homes. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A wind turbine uses large blades that catch the blowing wind. As the strong wind turns the blades, an internal generator converts this motion into electricity.

questions.question_text: Describe the basic process of weaving in the manufacturing of traditional clothes. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Weaving is the precise process of interlacing two distinct sets of yarn or threads at right angles to each other using a loom to form solid fabric.

questions.question_text: Explain why different parts of the Earth experience completely different seasons at the same time. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Seasons happen because the Earth is tilted on its axis. As it revolves around the Sun, different hemispheres tilt directly towards or away from the solar heat.

questions.question_text: Mention two simple, everyday ways students can help protect our shared home, the Earth. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Students can protect the Earth by turning off electrical switches when leaving a room and planting native tree saplings in their neighborhood to increase green cover.

questions.question_text: Imagine you visit a bustling traditional cotton textile mill. Describe the sights and sounds of the clothing manufacturing process you observe there. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I see huge bales of fluffy white cotton being fed into large, noisy machines. The rhythmic clacking of wooden looms fills the air as fast-moving shuttles weave thin spun threads into long, colorful rolls of beautiful fabric, ready to be dyed and stitched.

questions.question_text: Imagine a world where the 'Rhythms of Nature' like changing seasons completely stop forever. Describe how this sudden change would affect animals and human farming. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: If seasons completely stopped, farmers would not know when to plant or harvest crops, causing severe global food shortages. Animals that rely on migration or hibernation would lose their natural cues, leading to chaos in their survival patterns and disrupting entire food chains.

questions.question_text: Explain how shifting from polluting fossil fuels to renewable energy sources can create a much healthier environment for all living beings on Earth. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Burning fossil fuels like coal and oil releases harmful smoke and dangerous greenhouse gases that pollute the air and trap heat. By switching to renewable sources like solar and wind energy, we can significantly reduce air pollution, slow down global warming, and ensure cleaner air and a much safer climate for all plants, animals, and humans.

questions.question_text: Write a short pledge outlining three specific, practical actions you and your classmates will take to protect 'Earth Our Shared Home' in your daily school lives. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: We pledge to always carry reusable cloth bags and lunchboxes to school instead of using single-use plastics. We will ensure zero food wastage in our cafeteria and properly separate wet and dry garbage in the bins. Finally, we promise to save every drop of water by quickly turning off any running taps we find in the washrooms.
